# 2025 World Seniors Championship The **2025 World Seniors Championship** (officially the **2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Championship**) was a snooker tournament played from 7 to 11 May 2025 at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, England . It was the 16th edition of the World Seniors Championship and the seventh consecutive year the tournament was held at the Crucible . The event was open to players over 40 years of age who were not ranked inside the top 64 of the professional world rankings . The tournament was won by Alfie Burden, who defeated the 2018 champion Aaron Canavan 8–4 in the final to claim his first World Seniors title . Burden had previously finished as runner-up in the 2023 edition . The defending champion was Igor Figueiredo, who was eliminated in the first round by Wayne Townsend . The event was broadcast in the United Kingdom on Channel 5 . It was notable for marking the retirement of referee Michaela Tabb from traditional snooker officiating; she presided over the first session of the final before stepping down . ## Format and Participants The tournament featured a field of 16 players, consisting of invited legends, former world champions, and qualifiers from various international regions . The event was sponsored by the bookmaker JenningsBet . ### Qualification and Selection Participation was open to amateur players aged over 40 and professional players aged over 45, provided they were ranked outside the top 64 of the World Snooker Tour rankings . The field included: * **Defending Champion:** Igor Figueiredo (Brazil) . * **Former World Seniors Champions:** Jimmy White, Aaron Canavan . * **Invited Players:** Ken Doherty, Tony Drago, Tony Knowles . * **Debuting Professionals:** Joe Perry and Dominic Dale, both of whom announced their retirement from the professional tour prior to the event . * **Regional Qualifiers:** * **Europe:** Craig Steadman . * **Asia-Pacific:** Hassan Kerde (Australia) . * **Africa:** Charl Jonck (South Africa) . * **Americas:** Fabio Anderson Luersen (Brazil) . * **Golden Ticket Winner:** Alfie Burden (England), who qualified via a play-off event in Reading in April 2025 . * **Other Qualifiers:** Wayne Townsend, Andrew Norman, Gerard Greene . ### Match Format The format for the 2025 edition was expanded compared to previous years. The first round and quarter-finals were played as the best of 7 frames. The semi-finals were increased to the best of 11 frames, and the final was played as the best of 15 frames . ### Prize Fund The winner of the championship received a top prize of £15,000 . A special prize of a BYD SEAL U car was offered to the first player to compile a maximum break (147) during the tournament . ## Tournament Summary ### First Round The tournament began on 7 May 2025 . The opening round saw the elimination of the defending champion, Igor Figueiredo, who lost 2–4 to qualifier Wayne Townsend . Townsend secured the victory by winning the final three frames of the match . Two notable players making their World Seniors debut, Joe Perry and Dominic Dale, secured victories in their opening matches. Perry defeated Fabio Anderson Luersen 4–2, while Dale overcame Craig Steadman by the same scoreline . In a repeat of the 2023 final, Alfie Burden faced four-time winner Jimmy White. Burden defeated White 4–1, reversing the result of their previous title encounter . Ken Doherty, the 1997 World Champion, was defeated 2–4 by the African Seniors champion Charl Jonck . The Australian qualifier Hassan Kerde whitewashed Tony Knowles 4–0, while Tony Drago defeated Gerard Greene 4–3 in a deciding frame . The 2018 champion Aaron Canavan defeated Andrew Norman 4–1 . ### Quarter-finals In the quarter-finals, Dominic Dale defeated Joe Perry 4–1 in a match between the two recent professional retirees . Aaron Canavan eliminated Wayne Townsend 4–2 to advance to the semi-finals . Alfie Burden recovered from a 0–3 deficit against Tony Drago to win 4–3. Drago had won the second and third frames on a re-spotted black but was unable to secure the fourth frame required for victory . Hassan Kerde became the first Australian to reach the semi-finals of the World Seniors Championship by defeating Charl Jonck 4–2 . ### Semi-finals The semi-finals were played on 10 May as best-of-11 frame matches . Alfie Burden defeated Hassan Kerde 6–2. Burden established an early 4–0 lead with breaks of 57 and 65. Although Kerde won two frames to narrow the score, Burden secured the victory with a break of 97 in the seventh frame followed by a win in the eighth . The second semi-final between Aaron Canavan and Dominic Dale went to a deciding frame. Dale led 5–2 and compiled two century breaks during the match, including a 131 which stood as the highest break of the tournament. However, Canavan won four consecutive frames to win the match 6–5 . ### Final The final took place on 11 May 2025 between Alfie Burden and Aaron Canavan . It was the second appearance in the final for both players; Canavan had won the title in 2018, while Burden was the runner-up in 2023 . The match was officiated by Michaela Tabb and Proletina Velichkova. Tabb refereed the first five frames before retiring from professional snooker refereeing; she was recognized by the crowd and commentators for her 24-year career . Canavan won the opening frame, but Burden took the next four to lead 4–1 at the first interval . Burden extended his lead to 7–2, placing him one frame away from victory. Canavan mounted a brief recovery, winning two frames to reduce the deficit to 7–4. In the 12th frame, Burden made a break of 76 to secure an 8–4 victory . Following the match, Burden described the win as a "massive journey" and dedicated the victory to his supporters . ## Main Draw The results for the tournament were as follows :

Alfie Burden is the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Champion
=======================================================

[May 11, 2025May 11, 2025](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/05/11/alfie-burden-is-the-2025-world-seniors-snooker-champion/) [seniorsnooker](https://seniorsnooker.com/author/seniorsnooker/) [Event info](https://seniorsnooker.com/category/event-info/), [Player info](https://seniorsnooker.com/category/player-info/)[Event](https://seniorsnooker.com/tag/event/), [Player](https://seniorsnooker.com/tag/player/)

Alfie Burden beat Aaron Canavan by 8 frames to 4 this afternoon to become the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Champion. The match was played in good spirit … and an unusual format. Indeed it featured two intervals – after four and eight frames – and was refereed by Michaela Tab, before the first interval, and by Proletina Velichkova after the first interval to the finish.

**Michaela is retiring from snooker** but will continue to referee in the “900” competitions for the time being.

**Thank you for everything Michaela! We love you!**
---------------------------------------------------

It was an emotional win for Alfie who had lost in the 2023 Final to Jimmy White. Lifting the trophy, surrounded by his children and friends meant everything to Alfie and it showed! His opponent, Aaron Canavan, who had won this title in 2018, was the first to congratulate him.. Aaron is a great player and a huge credit to his sport: at the table he gives it is all, when the match is over, win or lose, he’s always gracious.

**Congratulations Alfie Burden**!
---------------------------------

**and to Aaron Canavan**, for a great run and for being such a great sportsman.

![Image 1](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-4.png?w=1024)

**Image by Zheng Zai**

Click here for more information.") From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
2025 World Seniors Championship
Tournament information
Dates7–11 May 2025
VenueCrucible Theatre
CitySheffield
CountryEngland
OrganisationWorld Seniors Tour
FormatSeniors event
Highest break Dominic Dale (WAL) (131)
Final
Champion Alfie Burden (ENG)
Runner-up Aaron Canavan (JEY)
Score8–4

← 2024

The **2025 World Seniors Championship** (officially the **2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Championship**) was a [snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker "Snooker") tournament that took place from 7 to 11 May 2025 at the [Crucible Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucible_Theatre "Crucible Theatre") in [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"), England, the seventh consecutive year that the tournament was held at the venue. Open to amateur players over 40 and professional players who were over 45 and also ranked outside the top 64 in the [snooker world rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker_world_rankings "Snooker world rankings"), the event was the 16th edition of the [World Seniors Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship "World Seniors Championship"), first held in [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_World_Seniors_Championship "1991 World Seniors Championship"). Organised by the [World Seniors Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Tour "World Seniors Tour"), the event was broadcast in the United Kingdom by [Channel 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_/(British_TV_channel/) "5 (British TV channel)") and internationally by other broadcasters. [Igor Figueiredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Figueiredo "Igor Figueiredo") was the defending champion, having defeated [Ken Doherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Doherty "Ken Doherty") 5‍–‍2 in the [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Seniors_Championship "2024 World Seniors Championship") final, but he lost 2‍–‍4 to Wayne Townsend in the first round. [Alfie Burden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfie_Burden "Alfie Burden") held leads of 4‍–‍1 and 7‍–‍2 against [Aaron Canavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan") in the final and went on to win 8‍–‍4 to claim his first World Seniors title. The tournament produced five [century breaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_break "Century break"), four of which were compiled by [Dominic Dale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Dale "Dominic Dale"), who also made the highest, a 131 in his semi-final match against Canavan. The final of the event was [Michaela Tabb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb "Michaela Tabb")'s last appearance as a traditional snooker referee, following a 24-year career during which she had refereed two [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Championship "World Snooker Championship") finals. [![Image 6: The Crucible Theatre from outside](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Sheffield_Crucible_theatre.png/330px-Sheffield_Crucible_theatre.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sheffield_Crucible_theatre.png) For the seventh consecutive year, the main stage of the tournament was held at the [Crucible Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucible_Theatre "Crucible Theatre") in [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"), England. The 2025 World Seniors Championship was a [snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker "Snooker") tournament that took place from 7 to 11 May 2025 at the [Crucible Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucible_Theatre "Crucible Theatre") in [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"), England.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2) The 16th edition of the [World Seniors Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship "World Seniors Championship"), first played in [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_World_Seniors_Championship "1991 World Seniors Championship"),[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-3) it was held at the Crucible for the seventh consecutive year[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-12) and sponsored by bookmaker JenningsBet.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1) A [World Seniors Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Tour "World Seniors Tour") event, the tournament was open to amateur players over 40 and professional players over 45, who also needed to be ranked outside the top 64 in the [snooker world rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker_world_rankings "Snooker world rankings").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-13) The event was broadcast in the United Kingdom on [Channel 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_/(British_TV_channel/) "5 (British TV channel)") and by other broadcasters internationally.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2) [Igor Figueiredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Figueiredo "Igor Figueiredo") was the defending champion, having defeated [Ken Doherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Doherty "Ken Doherty") 5‍–‍2 in the [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Seniors_Championship "2024 World Seniors Championship") final.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2024-14) Four referees officiated: Mark Beale, [Michaela Tabb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb "Michaela Tabb"), Rod Eaton, and Proletina Velichkova.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-15) Figueiredo, as the defending champion,[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2024-14) and was given the top [seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seeding_/(sports/) "Seeding (sports)").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WSTlineup-16) Other seeded players were Doherty, four-time winner of the event [Jimmy White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_White "Jimmy White"), [Tony Drago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Drago "Tony Drago") and [Tony Knowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Knowles_/(snooker_player/) "Tony Knowles (snooker player)"). [Joe Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Perry_/(snooker_player/) "Joe Perry (snooker player)") and [Dominic Dale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Dale "Dominic Dale") retired as professional players after their defeats in the qualifying stages of the [2025 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Snooker_Championship "2025 World Snooker Championship"), making them eligible to compete. Several players had to qualify. The winner of the [2018 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_World_Seniors_Championship "2018 World Seniors Championship"), [Aaron Canavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan"), as well as [Andrew Norman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Norman_/(snooker_player/) "Andrew Norman (snooker player)"), [Gerard Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Greene "Gerard Greene") and Townsend, qualified for the event during the so-called Race to the Crucible Series. Four more players qualified through various continental Seniors Championships: [Craig Steadman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Steadman "Craig Steadman") won in Europe, Hassan Kerde in Asia-Pacific, Charl Jonck in Africa and Fabio Luersen in the Americas.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WSTlineup-16) [Alfie Burden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfie_Burden "Alfie Burden") defeated Andy Lavin, [Rodney Goggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Goggins "Rodney Goggins"), Stuart Watson and Matthew Ford to win the Golden Ticket tournament to qualify for the final stages.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WSTBurden-17) The winner of the event received £20,000, with the runner-up earning £10,000.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2) [![Image 7: photo of Dominic Dale](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Dominic_Dale_PHC_2016-2.jpg/250px-Dominic_Dale_PHC_2016-2.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dominic_Dale_PHC_2016-2.jpg) [![Image 8: photo of Joe Perry](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/Joe_Perry_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28DerHexer%29_2013-01-31_01.jpg/250px-Joe_Perry_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28DerHexer%29_2013-01-31_01.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Perry_at_Snooker_German_Masters_/(DerHexer/)_2013-01-31_01.jpg) The first round took place on 7 and 8 May, each match played as the best of 7 [frames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#frame "Glossary of cue sports terms").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2) [Joe Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Perry_/(snooker_player/) "Joe Perry (snooker player)") made two breaks of 76 to take a 2‍–‍0 lead against Fabio Luersen and also compiled a 94 and a 59 to win 4‍–‍2.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-18)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19) "I was a little bit nervous which I was pleased about, I didn't want to be flat and not care," Perry said. [Craig Steadman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Steadman "Craig Steadman") recovered from 0‍–‍2 against [Dominic Dale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Dale "Dominic Dale") to tie the scores, but Dale then won the fifth frame and compiled a [century break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_break "Century break") of 107 in the sixth to clinch a 4‍–‍2 victory.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-20) "To win a tournament at the Crucible would be fantastic—it's a special place to play," Dale said. Wayne Townsend won the first frame of the match against the defending champion, [Igor Figueiredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Figueiredo "Igor Figueiredo"), with a break of 53 and on the final [black ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#black_ball "Glossary of cue sports terms"). Figueiredo replied with a half-century of his own and then took the lead at 2‍–‍1. Townsend won three frames on the spin, the last one again on the final black, to seal victory.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-FigueiredoTownsend-21)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19) "I'm on cloud nine. I was playing the world champion and I've knocked him out! There's no reason why I can't be the world champion and there is nobody here I can't beat," Townsend said after the match.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19) [Aaron Canavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan") manufactured breaks of 51, 89, 72 and 51 to defeat [Andrew Norman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Norman_/(snooker_player/) "Andrew Norman (snooker player)") 4‍–‍1.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-22) "If you enjoy it then the chances are that you will play better," Canavan conceded afterwards.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19) [Alfie Burden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfie_Burden "Alfie Burden") faced [Jimmy White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_White "Jimmy White"), winner of the event in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_World_Seniors_Championship "2010 World Seniors Championship"), [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_World_Seniors_Championship "2019 World Seniors Championship"), [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_World_Seniors_Championship "2020 World Seniors Championship") and [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Seniors_Championship "2023 World Seniors Championship").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WSTlineup-16) Burden won the first two frames, but White produced a 82 break in the third to halve the deficit. Burden won the fourth frame on the [re-spotted black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#re-spotted_black "Glossary of cue sports terms") and manufactured a 92 break in the fifth to advance into the quarter-finals.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WhiteBurden-23)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) Burden commented after the match that he had first practiced with White when he was 15 years old and that he was sure White would want him to go on to win the tournament now: "We've had this amazing friendship for many years and I don't get any pleasure in beating Jimmy \[White\] but I was focused on winning and I had to blank out who I was playing."[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) [Ken Doherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Doherty "Ken Doherty") took a 2‍–‍0 lead against Charl Jonck, but Jonck went on to win four consecutive frames, featuring breaks of 64 and 63, to win the match.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-25)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) "That was surreal. It was the lifelong ambition becoming a reality," Jonck said.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) [Tony Drago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Drago "Tony Drago") compiled a 75 break in the first frame of his duel with [Gerard Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Greene "Gerard Greene"). The match went into a [decider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#deciding_frame "Glossary of cue sports terms"), which Drago won aided by a break of 68.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-DragoGreene-26)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) Hassan Kerde [whitewashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitewash_/(sport/) "Whitewash (sport)") [Tony Knowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Knowles_/(snooker_player/) "Tony Knowles (snooker player)"), making breaks of 53, 62, 66 and 59 in the process.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-27)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) "I'm over the moon. I've watched the Crucible for the last 20 years and to just come and watch a match would have been awesome," Kerde said afterwards.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) The quarter-finals took place on 9 May, each match played as the best of 7 frames.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2) Dale compiled breaks of 97, 99 and 128 as he beat Perry 4‍–‍1.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-28) "I've been practicing hard here and I've found some form. I was confident going into the match," Dale commented.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-quarters-29) In his match against Burden, Drago won the first frame and then took two consecutive frames on the re-spotted black to edge 3‍–‍0 in front. Burden won four on the spin, featuring breaks of 53 and 51, to advance into the semi-finals.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-DragoBurden-30)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-quarters-29) Kerde and Jonck shared the first four frames, but Kerde then took two, one of them with a break of 85, to win the match.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-31) "I'm the first person to come from Australia and reach the semi-finals of the World Seniors Snooker Championship and hopefully I can do the country proud," Kerde said.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-quarters-29) Canavan took a 3‍–‍1 lead against Townsend, who compiled an 85 break in the fifth frame to halve the deficit. Canavan went on to take the following frame and seal victory with a 4‍–‍2 result.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-CanavanTownsend-32) The semi-finals took place on 10 May, both matches played as the best of 11 frames.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2) Burden produced breaks of 57 and 65 as he took a 4‍–‍0 lead against Kerde. Kerde replied by winning two consecutive frames and halving the deficit, but Burden made a break of 97 to go 5‍–‍2 in front and won the following frame to clinch victory.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-BurdenKerde-33)[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-semis-34) "It was a tough game but I was pleased with the way I played and it stands me in good stead for the final," Burden said afterwards.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-BurdenKerde-33) Canavan and Dale shared the first four frames of their semi-final. Dale then made back-to-back century breaks, of 109 and 131, and won another frame to go within one of victory at 5‍–‍2. Canavan, however, won four consecutive frames, including the decider, to book a place in the final.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-CanavanDale-35)[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-semis-34) "It was tough. After last night, I was really tired but I gave myself a good talking to in the dressing room and came out fighting," Canavan confessed.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-semis-34) [![Image 9: Alfie Burden playing a shot](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Alfie_Burden_and_Thorsten_M%C3%BCller_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28DerHexer%29_2015-02-05_01.jpg/250px-Alfie_Burden_and_Thorsten_M%C3%BCller_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28DerHexer%29_2015-02-05_01.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alfie_Burden_and_Thorsten_M%C3%BCller_at_Snooker_German_Masters_/(DerHexer/)_2015-02-05_01.jpg) [Alfie Burden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfie_Burden "Alfie Burden") _(pictured in 2015)_ defeated [Aaron Canavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan") 8‍–‍4 in the final to claim his first [World Seniors Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship "World Seniors Championship") title. On 11 May, Burden and Canavan contested the best-of-15-frame final, which was divided into three mini-sessions of five frames each.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Burden.Win-36) Both players were competing in a World Seniors final for the second time, Canavan having won the title in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_World_Seniors_Championship "2018 World Seniors Championship") and Burden having been runner-up in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Seniors_Championship "2023 World Seniors Championship"). The first five-frame mini-session was refereed by [Michaela Tabb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb "Michaela Tabb"), who retired from traditional snooker refereeing after the tournament, following a 24-year career that had included two [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Championship "World Snooker Championship") finals.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Burden.Win-36)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-37) Canavan won the opening frame, but Burden then won four consecutive frames with breaks including 74 and 54 as he moved 4–1 ahead.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Burden.Win-36) Proletina Velichkova refereed the remainder of the final.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-38) Canavan won the first frame of the second mini-session, but Burden took three consecutive frames with breaks of 65, 109, and 80. Canavan won the 8th frame to leave Burden leading 7–3. The third and final mini-session lasted two frames, as Canavan won frame 11 but Burden made a 76 break in the 12th to secure an 8–4 victory and win his first World Seniors title. He said afterwards: "I'm absolutely delighted. I thought I played well in the final. It's been a massive journey with so many ups and downs. I think it's been well documented that I think I've underachieved in my career but you've got to enjoy this moment."[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Burden.Win-36) The results for the main draw are shown below. Match winners are shown in bold. Numbers in parentheses after the players' names are [seedings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seeding_/(sports/) "Seeding (sports)").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2)[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-39)[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-PIKEFINAL-40)

Today’s final at the Crucible will be competed between two players who have been here before: Aaron Canavan, who won the title in 2018, and Alfie Burden who was runner-up in 2023.

[Here is how the semi-finals unfolded as reported by WSS](https://seniorssnooker.com/burden-and-canavan-set-up-world-final-meeting/):

> **Burden and Canavan Set Up World Final Meeting**
> -------------------------------------------------
> 
> **Alfie Burden and Aaron Canavan will meet in the final of the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship on Sunday afternoon.**
> 
> The two former finalists reached the title match by overcoming Hassan Kerde and Dominic Dale respectively on a memorable semi-final Saturday at the iconic Crucible Theatre.
> 
> ![Image 1](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image.png?w=1024)
> 
> Canavan heads into the title match aiming to become only the second multiple champion of the most prestigious event in seniors snooker, after four-time winner Jimmy White, while Burden hopes to go one step further than he did in 2023 when he ended as runner-up to ‘The Whirlwind’.
> 
> Former professional Burden and Asia-Pacific Seniors champion Kerde, from Australia, kicked off a bumper session with a best-of-11 frame contest.
> 
> ![Image 2](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-1.png?w=1024)
> 
> Burden was in fine form and he wasted no time in racing into a 4-0 lead with breaks of 57 and 65. The Australian briefly rallied, taking back-to-back frames to half the deficit, but a rapid-fire contribution of 97 put Burden back in the acendency and he secured his place in the final by taking the next frame.
> 
> Post-match, Burden said: “It was a tough game but I was pleased with the way I played and it stands me in good stead for the final. I’ve prepared well, practiced hard and I feel confident. I feel really strong – I’m going out and expecting to win tomorrow.”
> 
> ![Image 3](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-2.png?w=1024)
> 
> The second semi-final of the afternoon saw Canavan face Dale and, after sharing the first four frames of the contest, ‘The Spaceman’ appeared to step up a gear and fired in back-to-back century breaks of 109 and 131 before moving one frame from victory by taking the seventh.
> 
> The man from Jersey refused to go away, however, and managed to take the next three frames with a top visit of 65 to force an unlikely deciding frame.
> 
> ![Image 4](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-3.png?w=1024)
> 
> The decider was a nervy affair with both players spurning golden opportunities for the win. Ultimately, it was Canavan who took it on the colours to complete a famous comeback and set up a final meeting with Burden.
> 
> Canavan said: “It was tough. After last night, I was really tired but I gave myself a good talking to in the dressing room and came out fighting. It’s dream, you never think that you will get there and then all of a sudden something happens and you’re actually living the dream.”

World Seniors Snooker Championship: 2025 draw, preview, schedule
================================================================

by [David Caulfield](https://snookerhq.com/author/snookerhq/ "Posts by David Caulfield") on May 7, 2025

**The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship will take place this week with the likes of Igor Figueiredo and Jimmy White in the draw.**

The prestigious event on the World Seniors Snooker Tour will return to the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield for the seventh year in a row from May 7th to 11th.

There will be 16 players in the field this year, with Brazil’s Figueiredo representing the top seed as the [reigning champion](https://snookerhq.com/2024/05/12/igor-figueiredo-wins-world-seniors-snooker-championship/) and record four-time winner White on the opposite side of the draw.

Who is in the 2025 World Seniors Championship draw?
---------------------------------------------------

Joining Figeuredo and White will be a high-quality group of players in what is a very competitive lineup for an edition of the World Seniors Snooker Championship.

Figueiredo will launch his defence against Wayne Townsend, with White first in action against Alfie Burden in a repeat of the 2023 final.

It was recently announced that the Whirlwind would receive a [fresh two-year invitational card](https://snookerhq.com/2025/04/25/jimmy-white-receives-world-snooker-tour-lifeline/) to compete on the professional World Snooker Tour.

But the seniors circuit is where he has enjoyed the most success over the last decade or so, capturing a record eight titles and appearing in several other title-deciding encounters.

Elsewhere, two-time former world seniors runner-up Ken Doherty will face South African qualifier Charl Jonck with 2018 champion Aaron Canavan up against Andrew Norman.

Joining the World Seniors Tour in 2025 will be Joe Perry and Dominic Dale, meanwhile.

Both Perry and Dale confirmed their respective retirements from professional snooker in April after more than three decades on the main tour.

But neither has plans to give up the game entirely, and they will both represent serious threats to land the silverware in Sheffield.

Perry’s first outing of the competition will be against Fabio Anderson Luersen with Dale playing Craig Steadman, and the pair of former ranking event winners could clash as early as the quarter-finals.

One of the ties of the opening round sees Tony Drago – a semi-finalist in 2024 – meet Gerard Greene.

Tony Knowles is also back for another crack with the former world number two in action against Australian Hassan Kerde in the last 16.

The World Seniors Snooker Championship will take place at the iconic Crucible Theatre in Sheffield. Photo credit: [WSS](https://www.facebook.com/WorldSeniorsSnooker/photos_by)

Who are the betting favourites?
-------------------------------

Ken Doherty, a finalist last year and also the runner-up in 2020 when he blew a 4-0 lead in the final, is considered the outright betting favourite.

The Irishman has odds of 11/4 to go all the way to glory in the World Seniors Snooker Championship draw for the first time.

Joe Perry is next at 7/2 with Igor Figueiredo considered a 5/1 chance of securing successive successes in Sheffield.

The bookies have Jimmy White at only 6/1 in the outright betting market with [askgamblers.com](https://www.askgamblers.com/sports-betting/bonuses/free-bets) providing a list of popular sportbooks that have sign-up offers and free bets to avail of.

What is the format?
-------------------

It was announced that there will be an increase to the format this year, with longer matches adding to the drama that is bound to unfold.

The first two rounds will now be played over seven frames with 11 frames subsequently required for each semi-final.

The final on May 11th will then take place over 15 frames, marking a considerable increase from the previous best-of-nine finales.

How to watch the tournament?
----------------------------

Viewers in the United Kingdom and in some parts of Ireland will be able to watch the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship live on Channel 5.

Tickets are [still available](https://www.sheffieldtheatres.co.uk/events/world-seniors-snooker-championship-2025) for some sessions if you want to see the action in Sheffield up close and personal.

It was recently announced that the Crucible Theatre will continue to host the World Seniors Snooker Championship until at least 2027.

What happened last year?
------------------------

In 2024, an emotional Igor Figueiredo won one of the biggest titles of his career with a [5-2 victory over Ken Doherty](https://snookerhq.com/2024/05/12/igor-figueiredo-wins-world-seniors-snooker-championship/) in the final.

The affable Brazilian, who enjoyed several stints as a professional player on the World Snooker Tour, beat Tessa Davidson in round one before conjuring a standout victory over reigning champion Jimmy White in the quarter-finals.

A 4-1 success over Tony Drago in the penultimate round helped him through to the final showdown, where he duly overcame favourite Doherty.

The glory earned Figueiredo a £20,000 payday and also saw him receive a lucrative invitation to the prestigious Champion of Champions in Bolton.

Order of Play for 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship Announced
===============================================================================

11th April 2025

[Home](https://seniorssnooker.com/) » Order of Play for 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship Announced

**The order of play for the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship has been confirmed following yesterday’s draw made live on Channel 5.**

The event will take place at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield on 7-11 May with 16 players from nine nations competing for the flagship title on the World Seniors Snooker tour.

![Image 4](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/SeniorsDraw-300x169.jpg)

Every ball will be available to watch live on Channel 5 in the UK with a new, extended format announced for the 2025 edition of the competition which sees all matches up to the semi-finals stage now being best of seven frames while the semi-finals are now best of 11 and the final contested over the best of 15 frames.

The tournament begins on Wednesday afternoon with former ranking event champions Joe Perry and Dominic Dale making their respective World Seniors Snooker bows against Brazil’s Fabio Anderson Luersen and England’s Craig Steadman.

![Image 5](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/wednesday-8th-may-300x300.jpg)

Reigning champion Igor Figueiredo will begin the defence of his crown against Crucible debutant Wayne Townsend on Wednesday evening to be followed by fellow former World Seniors Snooker champion Aaron Canavan taking on Andrew Norman.

In what is sure to be a highly anticipated session on Thursday afternoon, four-time champion Jimmy ‘The Whirlwind’ White meets the winner of the upcoming Golden Ticket play-off before 1997 world champion Ken Doherty goes head-to-head with African Seniors champion Charl Jonck.

![Image 6](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/thursday-8th-may-300x300.jpg)

The opening round then concludes on Thursday evening with Tony ‘The Tornado’ Drago from Malta taking on Northern Ireland’s Gerard Green before Tony Knowles meets Australia’s Hassan Kerde.

The final will take place on Sunday 11 May.

[**Tickets remain available for the World Seniors Championship and start from just £17.50.**](https://www.sheffieldtheatres.co.uk/events/world-seniors-snooker-championship-2025)

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship – Quarter-Finals
============================================================

[May 10, 2025](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/05/10/the-2025-world-seniors-snooker-championship-quarter-finals/) [seniorsnooker](https://seniorsnooker.com/author/seniorsnooker/) [Uncategorized](https://seniorsnooker.com/category/uncategorized/)

These are the results of the quarter-finals yesterday at the Crucible:

![Image 1](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/canavan-4-2-townsend.png)

![Image 2](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/kerde-4-2-jonk.png)

![Image 3](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/burden-4-3-drago.png)

![Image 4](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/dale-4-1-perry.png)

Dominic entered the arena wearing a long fur coat and a hat… apparently a tribute to Alex Higgins. I know that Jason Francis started the Seniors tour because of Alex, who he wanted to help but I also know he quickly had to give up on the man who couldn’t really play anymore. But Alex game wasn’t the main issue, it’s his behaviour that caused a lot of problems … as had been the case all his life. Alex certainly changed snooker forever but, in my eyes, he was a terrible person and reading his bios didn’t change my opinion, quite the opposite. Anyway … back to yesterday action … as you can see by the scores, Dominic played very well and, despite winning frame 2, Joe was never really in the match.

Neither Alfie nor Tony scored really heavily in their match. There was no break over 53 in the match, and 53 isn’t usually enough in itself to secure a frame. But … what a battle this was. They played all seven frames and every frame was close and hard-fought. Tony was gutted and, I guess, Alfie was more relieved than really happy.

Hassan Kerde and Charl Jonk probably served us the best match on the day. Both played well, especially considering that neither had played at the Crucible before this event. A very happy Hassan was interviewed after the match, accompanied by his wife. They are Muslims and she was fully covered, wearing a long dress, and a scarf that completely covered her hair … but she was with him on the floor, all smiles, filming his interview with a very state of the art smartphone … 😊

The last match of the day was a late, rather scrappy affair. Wayne made the only big break of the match, a 85 but lost by 4-2. Both can play better but it was late and they had to wait a long time before the table became available for them. Aaron has won this title before and, maybe, that helped him. Unlike Wayne, he isn’t in uncharted territory here at the Crucible.

Here are the images I took on the day…

![Image 5](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2025seniors-5717.jpg)

Maximum Break Prize at the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship
==================================================================

[May 5, 2025](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/05/05/maximum-break-prize-at-the-2025-world-seniors-snooker-championship/) [seniorsnooker](https://seniorsnooker.com/author/seniorsnooker/) [Event info](https://seniorsnooker.com/category/event-info/)[Event](https://seniorsnooker.com/tag/event/)

BYD Lookers Sheffield is offering a “Maximum Break Prize” at the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship and it’s a very “traditional” prize as well, reminiscent of the old days… [here is the announcement](https://seniorssnooker.com/byd-lookers-sheffield-offer-maximum-break-prize-at-jenningsbet-world-seniors-snooker-championship/?fbclid=IwY2xjawKFPdtleHRuA2FlbQIxMQBicmlkETByTnFJcmFwUENOdXpGSlp2AR7Qer4MHcTqWVNyQUwbobc7WQ-C3lJV21kc3nOimGW8NJIu3lp4J5es88D-mg_aem_rltH53mel865IKS4ICF_2g):

> BYD Lookers Sheffield Offer Maximum Break Prize at JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship
> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
> 
> ****World Seniors Snooker (WSS) is pleased to announce a partnership with BYD Lookers Sheffield which will see a BYD SEAL U awarded to the first player to make a maximum break in this year’s JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship.****
> 
> The BYD SEAL U applies captivating design philosophy to the SUV market by combining the oceanic aesthetics of BYD design with futuristic touches, resulting in a striking car for eco-conscious families.
> 
> Jason Francis, Chairman of WSS, said: “The JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship celebrates legacy and memories, honouring former legends and creating new ones. For many, the historical prize for a 147 break was always a car and so we are delighted to partner with BYD Lookers Sheffield to offer this fantastic prize.”
> 
> ![Image 1](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-6.png?w=700)
> 
> Ryan Smith, General Manager of BYD Lookers Sheffield said “It’s great for BYD Sheffield to be involved with the World Seniors Snooker Championship and to showcase our brand at the famous Crucible Theatre live on Channel 5.”
> 
> The car on offer will be displayed outside the Crucible Theatre during the event and fans will be able to view it and book a test drive with BYD Lookers Sheffield.
> 
> [**Learn more about BYD Lookers Sheffield.**](https://www.lookers.co.uk/byd)

Jennings Bet World Seniors Championship 2025

← 2024

 
Die **Jennings Bet [World Seniors Championship](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship "World Seniors Championship") 2025** war ein [Snookerturnier](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker "Snooker") der World Seniors Tour. Vom 7. bis 11. Mai wurde, wie in den Jahren zuvor, unmittelbar nach der [Weltmeisterschaft](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snookerweltmeisterschaft_2025 "Snookerweltmeisterschaft 2025") der Profitour im [Crucible Theatre](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucible_Theatre "Crucible Theatre") von [Sheffield](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield") die WM der Seniorentour gespielt. Der Wettanbieter Jennings war in der 16. Ausgabe des Turniers der 10. Sponsor. Titelverteidiger [Igor Figueiredo](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Figueiredo "Igor Figueiredo") unterlag in Runde 1. [Alfie Burden](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Burden "Alfred Burden"), [2023](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2023 "World Seniors Championship 2023") bereits Vizeweltmeister der Senioren, gewann bei seinem zweiten WM-Auftritt den Weltmeistertitel. Er besiegte [Aaron Canavan](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan"), den Seniorenweltmeister von [2018](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2018 "World Seniors Championship 2018"), im Endspiel mit 8:4. Neben dem Titelverteidiger [Igor Figueiredo](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Figueiredo "Igor Figueiredo") traten Rekordtitelträger [Jimmy White](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_White "Jimmy White") und Ex-Weltmeister [Ken Doherty](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Doherty "Ken Doherty") im Turnier an. [Joe Perry](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Perry_/(Snookerspieler/) "Joe Perry (Snookerspieler)") und [Dominic Dale](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Dale "Dominic Dale") hatten beide ihre Profikarriere nach der Weltmeisterschaft 2025 beendet und waren erstmals bei den Senioren am Start. Daneben erhielten auch [Tony Drago](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Drago "Tony Drago") und [Tony Knowles](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Knowles_/(Snookerspieler/) "Tony Knowles (Snookerspieler)") eine Einladung. Die vier Kontinental-Seniorenmeister waren ebenfalls ins Teilnehmerfeld aufgenommen worden: * [Craig Steadman](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Steadman "Craig Steadman") ([European Seniors Champion](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/EBSA-Senioren-Snookereuropameisterschaft "EBSA-Senioren-Snookereuropameisterschaft")) * [Fabio Anderson Luersen](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabio_Luersen "Fabio Luersen") ([Pan American Seniors Champion](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/PABSA-Snooker-Amerikameisterschaft#Sieger "PABSA-Snooker-Amerikameisterschaft")) * [Charl Jonck](https://de.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Charl_Jonck&action=edit&redlink=1 "Charl Jonck (Seite nicht vorhanden)") (African Seniors Champion) * Hassan Kerde (Asia-Pacific Seniors Champion) Dazu gab es die „Race to the Crucible Series“ mit neun Qualifikationsturnieren. Die vier besten Spieler der Gesamtwertung waren direkt qualifiziert. Weitere 16 Spieler spielten ein Play-off um das fünfte „Golden Ticket“: * [Aaron Canavan](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan") (1. Qualifikant) * [Andrew Norman](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Norman "Andrew Norman") (2. Qualifikant) * [Gerard Greene](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Greene "Gerard Greene") (3. Qualifikant) * Wayne Townsend (4. Qualifikant) * [Alfie Burden](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Burden "Alfred Burden") (Golden Ticket)[\[1\]](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2025#cite_note-Burden-1) Eine Teilnehmerin aus dem Frauensnooker wie im Vorjahr gab es nicht. Eine wesentliche Änderung war die Verlängerung der Distanzen: Bereits in den ersten beiden Runden wurde [Best of 7](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best-of-Modus "Best-of-Modus") statt Best of 5 gespielt. Im Halbfinale kamen bis zu 4 Frames hinzu und das Finale war Best of 15 (8 Gewinnframes) statt wie bislang Best of 9 (5 Gewinnframes).[\[2\]](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2025#cite_note-Teilnehmer-2)[\[3\]](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2025#cite_note-Spielplan-3)[\[4\]](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2025#cite_note-Termine-4)[\[5\]](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2025#cite_note-Ergebnisse-5)

Beide Spieler hatten Finalerfahrung. [Aaron Canavan](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan") hatte [2018](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2018 "World Seniors Championship 2018") den Titel gewonnen und kam als Nummer 1 der Seniorenweltrangliste.[\[6\]](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2025#cite_note-Ranking-6) Im Halbfinale hatte er mit [Dominic Dale](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Dale "Dominic Dale") einen Titelfavoriten geschlagen. [Alfie Burden](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Burden "Alfred Burden") hatte [2023](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2023 "World Seniors Championship 2023") das Endspiel gegen [Jimmy White](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_White "Jimmy White") verloren, den er aber in Runde 1 bereits ausgeschaltet hatte. Burden hatte in der abgelaufenen Saison noch auf der [Profitour](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Tour "World Snooker Tour") gespielt, aber gerade seinen Tourplatz verloren. Im Finale gab es noch eine Besonderheit: Die populäre ehemalige Profischiedsrichterin [Michaela Tabb](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb "Michaela Tabb") beendete ihre offizielle Snookerkarriere. Sie leitete das erste Drittel der Partie und übergab dann an ihre Kollegin [Proletina Velichkova](https://de.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Proletina_Velichkova&action=edit&redlink=1 "Proletina Velichkova (Seite nicht vorhanden)"). Im ersten Drittel wurden bereits die Weichen gestellt. Zwar erkämpfte sich Canavan den ersten Frame, die folgenden vier Frames dominierte aber Burden, der seinem Gegner nur wenige Punkte ließ und selbst mit höheren Breaks überzeugte. Nach einer Pause und dem Wechsel der Schiedsrichterin hatte erneut der Mann von der Insel [Jersey](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey "Jersey") den besseren Start mit einem 75er Break, doch statt einer Aufholjagd gab es weitere hohe Breaks von Burden, der auf 7:2 davonzog und nur noch einen Frame vor dem Sieg stand. Canavan kämpfte, er rettete sich über die Pause ins letzte Drittel und konnte noch einen weiteren Frame gewinnen, dann entschied aber erneut ein hohes Break das Finale mit 8:4 zu Gunsten von Burden und brachte dem Engländer seinen ersten Titel im Seniorenbereich.[\[7\]](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship_2025#cite_note-Finale-7)

**The 2025 World Seniors Championship takes place at The Crucible, and you can follow the latest results and schedule of play here.**

The 16th edition of the tournament features 16 players aged over 40 competing at the sport’s spiritual home in Sheffield, just days after the conclusion of a thrilling World Championship.

This year’s field includes a host of former ranking event winners and qualifiers, as they battle it out for the title from May 7-11.

Igor Figueredo is the defending champion after he defeated Ken Doherty 5-2 in last year’s final to claim the crown for the first time.

Brazil’s Figueredo and 1997 World Champion Doherty are joined by four-time World Seniors Champion Jimmy White and 2018 champion Aaron Canavan.

Having recently announced their retirement from professional snooker, former Welsh Open champion Joe Perry and former Shanghai Masters champion Dominic Dale make their debut in the event.

Two-time ranking event winner Tony Knowles, last year’s semi-finalist Tony Drago and former main tour professionals Craig Steadman, Alfie Burden and Gerard Greene also feature.

First Round and Quarter-Final matches are to be contested over the best of seven frames, while Semi-Finals are best of 11 and the final best of 15.

Aaron Canavan is the 2025 Channel Islands Champion
==================================================

[July 1, 2025](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/07/01/aaron-canavan-is-the-2025-channel-islands-champion/) [seniorsnooker](https://seniorsnooker.com/author/seniorsnooker/) [Uncategorized](https://seniorsnooker.com/category/uncategorized/)

[Here is the report shared by WSF](https://worldsnookerfederation.org/champion-canavan-continues-channel-islands-snooker-dominance/?fbclid=IwY2xjawLQd5JleHRuA2FlbQIxMQBicmlkETByTnFJcmFwUENOdXpGSlp2AR6sfTrUGsOZxL36I-fwv_rbz5AneVbBpEM9XxUfNB44HjSyTtC7gWeb8myZsA_aem_X3Pq6sRl5CzNY4JW-3uhew)

> **Champion Canavan Continues Channel Islands Snooker Dominance**
> ----------------------------------------------------------------
> 
> **Jersey champion Aaron Canavan defeated Guernsey champion Paul Le Sauvage 5-0 to win the 2025 Channel Islands Snooker Championship.**
> 
> Canavan has now claimed the Channel Islands crown for each of the last four consecutive years. It is the 12th time overall that the 49-year-old has won the title and he maintains his 100% record of having never lost the unique champion v champion challenge match.
> 
> Pitching together the recent winners of the respective Jersey and Guernsey championships, the two biggest islands in the region take it in turns each year to host the encounter – this year it was held at the North Social Club in Saint Sampson, Guernsey.
> 
> Former world seniors champion Canavan took control of the tie early on, compiling a break of 71 on his way to securing the opening frame before doubling his lead. An effort of 50 helped him to a 3-0 advantage before he reached the hill with frame four. Canavan finished the contest in style, fashioning a run of 101 in the fifth frame to complete a whitewash.
> 
> This dozen of Channel Island triumphs came just days after he won an incredible 14th Jersey championship title.
> 
> For six consecutive years now, Canavan has conquered on the island.  What’s more, it is the third year in succession that he has not dropped a single frame en route to glory. The last time he relinquished a frame was during a last 16 match against Brett Campbell in the 2022 edition. Canavan’s last defeat in the competition was the 2019 final when he was ousted 4-3 by Gary Britton.
> 
> In this year’s title match staging, Canavan registered breaks of 60, 67 and 73 in a 4-0 victory over former winner Karl le Fevre. It was the third year in-a-row that the two had met in the final.
> 
> A few weeks after his latest domestic glories, Canavan went all the way to the final of the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship at the Crucible Theatre where he was stopped by Alfie Burden. In his semi-final match, Canavan produced a memorable comeback as he pipped Dominic Dale, 6-5, having been 5-2 down.
> 
> ![Image 1](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image.png?w=580)
> 
> **Le Sauvage completes hat-trick of Guernsey crowns after 24-year wait**
> ------------------------------------------------------------------------
> 
> Although the Channel Islands title would prove to be a step too far, Paul Le Sauvage can look back on a fantastic domestic campaign in Guernsey that saw him win his third island crown.
> 
> Winner of the Guernsey Snooker Championship in 1994 and 2001, Le Sauvage ended a 24-year wait for his hat-trick, rewriting the record books in the process with the longest gap between titles in the 94-year history of the competition.
> 
> In the early rounds of this year’s event, Le Sauvage eliminated Ali Gilliland 3-1, Kate Le Gallez 3-0, and John Skillet 4-3, before recovering from 3-1 behind to dethrone defending champion Adam Shorto 4-3 in the semi-finals. Shorto had lifted the trophy in each of the last two years.
> 
> In the final at the North Social Club, Le Sauvage scored a 5-0 win over Roscoe Cloarec to regain the island’s top snooker prize.

**Congratulations Aaron Canavan**!
==================================

Click here for more information.") From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Michaela Tabb

Tabb refereeing in Berlin for the 2013 German Masters

Born11 December 1967 (age 58)
Bath, Somerset, England
Sport country Scotland
Professional2001–2015
**Michaela Tabb** (born 11 December 1967) is a Scottish [snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker "Snooker") and [pool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pool_/(cue_sports/) "Pool (cue sports)") referee. She established significant milestones for female officials in professional [cue sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cue_sports "Cue sports"), beginning in pool, where she officiated at top tournaments such as the [WPA World Nine-ball Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WPA_World_Nine-ball_Championship "WPA World Nine-ball Championship") and the [Mosconi Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosconi_Cup "Mosconi Cup"). She qualified in 2001 to referee on the [World Snooker Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Tour "World Snooker Tour") and was the sport's highest profile female referee for the next 14 years. She became the first woman to officiate at a professional ranking snooker tournament at the [2002 Welsh Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Welsh_Open_/(snooker/) "2002 Welsh Open (snooker)"), and the first woman to referee a ranking tournament final at the [2007 Welsh Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Welsh_Open_/(snooker/) "2007 Welsh Open (snooker)"). She was the first woman to referee the [World Snooker Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Championship "World Snooker Championship") final, which she did twice, in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Snooker_Championship "2009 World Snooker Championship") and [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_World_Snooker_Championship "2012 World Snooker Championship"). She remained the only woman to referee the World final until [Desislava Bozhilova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desislava_Bozhilova "Desislava Bozhilova") did so in the [2025 event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Snooker_Championship "2025 World Snooker Championship"). Tabb left the professional snooker tour in March 2015 following a dispute with the sport's commercial arm, [World Snooker Ltd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Tour "World Snooker Tour"), against which she brought a case alleging [sex discrimination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_discrimination "Sex discrimination"), [unfair dismissal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unfair_dismissal "Unfair dismissal"), and [breach of contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breach_of_contract "Breach of contract"). The parties reached an out-of-court settlement in September 2015, under which World Snooker Ltd paid Tabb an undisclosed financial sum. She continued to referee at pool events and on the [World Seniors Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Tour "World Seniors Tour"). In May 2025, following the [2025 World Seniors Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship "2025 World Seniors Championship"), she retired from refereeing standard snooker events. Tabb is also a former pool player. In the 1990s and early 2000s, she competed on the women's [eight-ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eight-ball "Eight-ball") pool circuit, where she won a number of titles as a solo competitor and as a member, and later captain, of the Scottish Ladies' Pool Team. Born on 11 December 1967, in [Bath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bath,_Somerset "Bath, Somerset"), England,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-WPBSA-1) Tabb moved to Scotland with her family when she was three years old.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Record_photoshoots-2) She studied chemistry, biology, and psychology at the [University of Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Glasgow "University of Glasgow"), dropping out before receiving a degree.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Ep5AP-3) Before becoming a full-time professional referee, she worked as a sales representative for a number of blue-chip companies.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Patterson99-4) She was also a sales representative for the [Ann Summers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Summers "Ann Summers") lingerie retailer.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Record_photoshoots-2) Tabb resides in [Dunfermline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunfermline "Dunfermline"), Scotland, with her husband, pool player [Ross McInnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_McInnes_/(pool_player/) "Ross McInnes (pool player)"), whom she met while they were playing on the men's and women's Scottish pool teams.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-:0-5) They have two sons, Morgan and Preston, both of whom play competitive pool; Morgan McInnes has played on Scotland's under-23 A team at the [European Pool Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Pool_Championships "European Pool Championships").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Pitt09-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-7) In July 2018, Tabb and her family established Blackball Tables, distributing pool tables and accessories.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-8) After running the business from their home for five years, they opened a store, On Cue World, in [Rosyth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosyth "Rosyth") in 2024.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-9) Tabb started playing competitive [blackball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackball_/(pool/) "Blackball (pool)") in 1991, at the age of 23. Selected the following year to play on the Scottish Ladies' Pool Team,[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Swarbrick04-10) she went on to captain the team to two consecutive Grand Slam titles in 1997 and 1998 by winning the Nations Cup, European Championships, and World Championships in the same season.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Patterson99-4) She remained on the team until 2003.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Patterson99-4) Her sister Juliette also played on the Scottish ladies' team.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-tost_Thel-11) As an individual competitor, Tabb won the UK women's singles title in 1997. The following year, she won the [European Pool Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Pool_Championships "European Pool Championships") held in [Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar "Gibraltar").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Pitt09-6)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-ladi_SPAL-12) Tabb began refereeing in the mid-1990s when she and her husband, Ross McInnes, began running amateur [eight-ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eight-ball "Eight-ball") and [nine-ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine-ball "Nine-ball") pool tournaments.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-tost_Thel-11) McInnes subsequently encouraged her to pursue refereeing professionally.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Swarbrick04-10) She made her professional refereeing debut at the St. Andrew's Cup nine-ball pool tournament in September 1997, while pregnant with her first son.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Hostility-13)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Pitt09-6) She refereed on television for the first time the following year, when the 1998 St. Andrew's Cup, sponsored by [Matchroom Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matchroom_Sport "Matchroom Sport"), was broadcast on [Sky Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_Sports "Sky Sports").[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Patterson98-14) She went on to become one of pool's top officials, refereeing at the [WPA World Nine-ball Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WPA_World_Nine-ball_Championship "WPA World Nine-ball Championship") and the [Mosconi Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosconi_Cup "Mosconi Cup").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Times09-15) In 2017 Tabb became the head referee on the [World Pool Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=World_Pool_Series&action=edit&redlink=1 "World Pool Series (page does not exist)").[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-JoinsWPS-16) [![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Michaela_Tabb_at_German_Masters_Snooker_Final_%28DerHexer%29_2012-02-05_05.jpg/330px-Michaela_Tabb_at_German_Masters_Snooker_Final_%28DerHexer%29_2012-02-05_05.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michaela_Tabb_at_German_Masters_Snooker_Final_/(DerHexer/)_2012-02-05_05.jpg) Tabb replacing the balls into their case during the [2012 German Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_German_Masters "2012 German Masters") final Stating that he wanted to change the dowdy, all-male image of [snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker "Snooker") referees, Jim McKenzie, then chief executive of the [World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Professional_Billiards_and_Snooker_Association "World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association"), recruited Tabb to referee snooker events in 2001.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Potter05-17) Exempted from the customary five-year refereeing apprenticeship, she qualified as a Class 3 snooker referee in September 2001.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-WPBSA-1) She conceded that this fast-tracking generated resentment among her fellow officials and referees.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Blackhurst03-18) On 23 January 2002, Tabb became the first woman to referee at a [professional ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker_world_rankings "Snooker world rankings") snooker tournament when she took charge of a first-round match between [Ken Doherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Doherty "Ken Doherty") and [James Wattana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Wattana "James Wattana") at the [2002 Welsh Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Welsh_Open_/(snooker/) "2002 Welsh Open (snooker)") in Newport.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-WPBSA-1) In [2003](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_World_Snooker_Championship "2003 World Snooker Championship"), she made her [World Snooker Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Championship "World Snooker Championship") debut at the [Crucible Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucible_Theatre "Crucible Theatre") in Sheffield, refereeing a first-round match between [Mark King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_King_/(snooker_player/) "Mark King (snooker player)") and [Drew Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drew_Henry "Drew Henry").[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Blackhurst03-18) In July 2003, dwindling sponsorship revenue forced the WPBSA to cut its tournament referees from ten to eight.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Potter05-17) Tabb's contract, along with that of Dutch referee Johan Oomen, was terminated on a last-in, first-out basis, threatening her future in the sport.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-insi_WORL-19) However, the WPBSA soon reversed its decision to dismiss Tabb and she signed a new contract in September 2003, along with Oomen.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Potter05-17) [![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Michaela_Tabb_at_German_Masters_Snooker_Final_%28DerHexer%29_2012-02-05_02.jpg/330px-Michaela_Tabb_at_German_Masters_Snooker_Final_%28DerHexer%29_2012-02-05_02.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Michaela_Tabb_at_German_Masters_Snooker_Final_/(DerHexer/)_2012-02-05_02.jpg) Tabb using a [triangle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#triangle "Glossary of cue sports terms") to rack the [red balls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#red_balls "Glossary of cue sports terms") On 18 February 2007, Tabb became the first woman to officiate at a ranking event final, taking charge as [Neil Robertson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Robertson "Neil Robertson") defeated [Andrew Higginson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Higginson_/(snooker_player/) "Andrew Higginson (snooker player)") 9–8 to win the [2007 Welsh Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Welsh_Open_/(snooker/) "2007 Welsh Open (snooker)").[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-time_Woma-20) On 20 January 2008, she refereed her first [Triple Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_Crown_/(snooker/) "Triple Crown (snooker)") final at the [2008 Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Masters_/(snooker/) "2008 Masters (snooker)"), which saw [Mark Selby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Selby "Mark Selby") defeat [Stephen Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Lee_/(snooker_player/) "Stephen Lee (snooker player)") 10–3.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-tost_Thel-11)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Hendon08-21) On 5 April 2009, she took charge of the [China Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_China_Open_/(snooker/) "2009 China Open (snooker)") final in Beijing, where [Peter Ebdon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Ebdon "Peter Ebdon") beat [John Higgins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Higgins "John Higgins") 10–8.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-news_BBCS-22)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-x9ZZT-23) Tabb became the first woman to referee a World Snooker Championship final in [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Snooker_Championship "2009 World Snooker Championship"),[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Hostility-13)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-Pitt09-6)[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-OAL3U-24) officiating as John Higgins defeated [Shaun Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaun_Murphy "Shaun Murphy") 18–9 to capture his third world title.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-tele_Worl-25)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-news_BBCS-22) She also refereed the [2012 World Snooker Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_World_Snooker_Championship "2012 World Snooker Championship") final, in which [Ronnie O'Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_O%27Sullivan "Ronnie O'Sullivan") defeated [Ali Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Carter "Ali Carter") 18–11 to win his fourth world title.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-l69kZ-26)[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-VGj3s-27) She remained the only female referee to have officiated at a world championship final until [Desislava Bozhilova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desislava_Bozhilova "Desislava Bozhilova") did so at the [2025 World Snooker Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Snooker_Championship "2025 World Snooker Championship") final.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-28) On 19 March 2015, [World Snooker Ltd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Tour "World Snooker Tour") announced that Tabb had left the professional refereeing circuit.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-cnZBT-29) In September 2015, appearing under her married name of Michaela McInnes, Tabb brought an [Employment Tribunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employment_Tribunal "Employment Tribunal") against World Snooker Ltd, claiming [sexual discrimination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_discrimination "Sexual discrimination"), [unfair dismissal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unfair_dismissal "Unfair dismissal") and [breach of contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breach_of_contract "Breach of contract").[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-fV7sK-30) World Snooker Ltd made an undisclosed out-of-court financial settlement.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-BjoSz-31) After leaving the main professional circuit, Tabb continued to referee [World Seniors Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Tour "World Seniors Tour") events,[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-JoinsWPS-16) including the [World Seniors Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship "World Seniors Championship") finals in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_World_Seniors_Championship "2019 World Seniors Championship"), [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_World_Seniors_Championship "2020 World Seniors Championship"), [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_World_Seniors_Championship "2022 World Seniors Championship"), [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Seniors_Championship "2023 World Seniors Championship") and [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship "2025 World Seniors Championship").[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-QE66h-32) On 11 May 2025, after refereeing the first session of the 2025 World Seniors Championship final, Tabb retired from refereeing standard snooker events, bringing to an end a 24-year career.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-33)[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-34) The professional snooker tour now features a significant number of female referees, including [Desislava Bozhilova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desislava_Bozhilova "Desislava Bozhilova"), [Maike Kesseler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maike_Kesseler "Maike Kesseler"), and [Tatiana Woollaston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatiana_Woollaston "Tatiana Woollaston"). Tabb has commented on her groundbreaking role in opening the sport up to female referees, saying: "I know that my legacy is that all these young ladies that I can see on the television are doing that job because I did it”.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_note-:0-5) 1. ^ [_**a**_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_ref-WPBSA_1-0) [_**b**_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_ref-WPBSA_1-1) [_**c**_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb#cite_ref-WPBSA_1-2) ["Profile – Michaela Tabb"](https://web.archive.org/web/20150402215127/http://www.worldsnooker.com/page/MichaelaTabb/0,,13165~2229999,00.html). World Snooker. Archived from [the original](http://www.worldsnooker.com/page/MichaelaTabb/0,,13165~2229999,00.html) on 2 April 2015. Line-Up Confirmed for 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship
=========================================================================

8th April 2025

[Home](https://seniorssnooker.com/) » Line-Up Confirmed for 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship

**Jimmy White, Ken Doherty and Igor Figueiredo headline a star-studded line-up at the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Championship which takes place at the Crucible Theatre on 7-11 May.**

![Image 4](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/D52_0411-300x200.jpg)

Brazil’s Figueiredo made history for South American snooker 12 months ago by winning the flagship title and he will begin the defence of his crown as the top seed on the opening Wednesday afternoon session.

Jimmy ‘The Whirlwind’ White will be aiming to win a record-extending fifth World Seniors Snooker Championship title at the sport’s most iconic venue and he gets underway on the afternoon of Thursday 8 May – as does the 1997 World champion Ken Doherty.

![Image 5](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/White2-300x200.jpg)

Former ranking event champions Joe Perry and Dominic Dale will make their World Seniors Snooker debuts at the event and they are joined as seeds by Malta’s Tony ‘The Tornado’ Drago, former world number two Tony Knowles and World Seniors Snooker’s world number one Aaron Canavan – who notably won the 2018 Championship.

Canavan is one of four players to have qualified via the ‘Race to the Crucible Series’ which saw players compete across nine events to earn their spots via the rankings. The man from Jersey is joined by Andrew Norman, Gerard Greene and Crucible debutant Wayne Townsend in qualifying via this route.

![Image 6](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/WS-Snooker-Poster-2025-FINAL-212x300.jpg)

Additionally, Craig Steadman, Hassan Kerde, Charl Jonck and Fabio Anderson Luersen will add to the international field having earned their right via the continental Seniors Championships in the Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa and Americas regions respectively.

One place remains up for grabs and this will go to the winner of the ‘Golden Ticket’ Play-Off which sees 16 players competing for the spot at The Crucible Club in Reading on 19-20 April. Click here to view the draw.

[**Tickets remains available for the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship and start from £17.50.**](https://www.sheffieldtheatres.co.uk/events/world-seniors-snooker-championship-2025)
